issues.t: Automatic transmission shifting poorly at high mileage
issues.sym: Late, harsh or slipping shifts, the engine revving up between gears, or the car feeling like it is stuck in one gear.
issues.why: The automatic transaxle wears internally with age. Owners most often report trouble somewhere past 110,000 miles, and old or low fluid makes it worse.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and color first. If it slips or won't shift, drive gently and get a transmission diagnosis before it leaves you stranded. On a car this old, a good used transmission is often the practical fix.

issues.t: Ignition coil inside the distributor fails
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, stalls without warning, misfires, or runs rough. It may get worse when the engine is hot.
issues.why: The Tercel's ignition coil sits inside the distributor. It wears out with heat and age, usually somewhere between about 95,000 and 180,000 miles, and stops sending a strong spark.
issues.next: Have a shop check for spark when the problem happens. Replacing the coil, or the whole distributor if the cap and rotor are also worn, usually fixes it.

issues.t: Starter fails and the engine won't crank
issues.sym: You turn the key and hear a single click, rapid clicking or nothing at all, even though the dash lights come on.
issues.why: The starter motor wears out at higher mileage. Owners commonly report it between about 110,000 and 160,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the battery and cables tested first, since a weak battery causes the same symptom. If they are good, the starter usually needs replacing.

issues.t: Failed emissions test from a clogged EGR system
issues.sym: The car fails a smog or emissions test for high NOx, or the check engine light comes on. Some cars ping or knock when accelerating.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system feeds a little exhaust back into the engine to lower emissions. Its valve and passages fill with carbon over time, usually after about 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check EGR flow. Cleaning the passages often fixes it; a stuck valve gets replaced. This is not urgent, but fix it before your next inspection.

issues.t: Rattle from the timing belt tensioner
issues.sym: A rattling or chattering noise from the passenger side of the engine, often loudest at idle.
issues.why: The timing belt tensioner and pulleys wear at high mileage, usually past 100,000 miles. A worn tensioner lets the belt run loose.
issues.next: Have the timing belt area inspected soon. If the belt is due or the tensioner is worn, replace the belt, tensioner and idler pulley together. A broken timing belt stops the engine right away.

issues.sym: Extra vibration at idle or in gear, or a clunk when you shift into drive or reverse or step on the gas.
issues.why: The rubber in the passenger-side engine mount breaks down with age and mileage, letting the engine move more than it should.
issues.next: Have the mounts checked during your next service. It is not an emergency, but a broken mount puts extra strain on hoses, wiring and the exhaust.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failing rear oxygen sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light is on and the car may fail an emissions test, but it usually drives normally.
issues.why: The oxygen sensor after the catalytic converter wears out with age and reports wrong readings to the engine computer.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If they point to the rear oxygen sensor, replacing it is a simple job. Confirm the catalytic converter is healthy before buying parts.

issues.t: Check engine light from the EVAP charcoal canister
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with an evaporative emissions (EVAP) code. You may smell fuel or have trouble filling the tank.
issues.why: The charcoal canister that traps fuel vapors can crack or clog with age, setting an EVAP fault.
issues.next: First make sure the gas cap is tight and its seal is not cracked. If the light comes back, have the EVAP system tested; replacing the canister is a common fix.

issues.t: Crankshaft sensor code (P0335) from a weak battery
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0335, sometimes after slow cranking or a hard start.
issues.why: Toyota found that low battery voltage while cranking can set this crankshaft position sensor code even when the sensor is fine.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested before replacing the sensor. A new battery often clears it for good.

issues.t: Rough idle and backfiring with the check engine light on
issues.sym: The engine shakes at idle, pops or backfires, and the check engine light is on.
issues.why: Owners report this on 1998 Tercels. Common causes on this engine are worn spark plugs or wires, a weak distributor coil, or a carbon-clogged idle air control valve.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the ignition system checked. If the light is flashing, drive as little as possible, because misfires can overheat the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Grinding when shifting into fifth gear
issues.sym: On manual-transmission cars, a grind or crunch when shifting into fifth, especially when shifting quickly.
issues.why: The synchronizer ring for fifth gear wears out at high mileage, so it can no longer match gear speeds smoothly.
issues.next: Make sure the clutch fully disengages and the gear oil is full and fresh. If it still grinds, the transmission needs a synchro repair; until then, shift into fifth slowly.

issues.t: Airbags did not deploy in a crash (owner reports)
issues.sym: Several owners told NHTSA the front airbags did not go off in frontal crashes. There may be no warning beforehand.
issues.why: No recall was issued and no cause was confirmed. A fault in the airbag (SRS) system, sensors or wiring can stop deployment, and the SRS warning light is the main clue.
issues.next: Watch the airbag light when you start the car: it should come on briefly, then go out. If it stays on, flashes or never lights, have the SRS system checked by a qualified shop soon.

issues.t: Seat belt won't latch or retract
issues.sym: A front seat belt won't click into the buckle, won't stay latched, or won't pull out or wind back in.
issues.why: Buckles and retractors wear and collect dirt after many years. Toyota also issued a bulletin about the 1996 front passenger belt and offered a longer belt.
issues.next: Do not carry a passenger in a seat whose belt won't latch. Have the buckle or retractor replaced; a dealer can check for any bulletin parts.

issues.sym: The heater blows lukewarm air, or the fan works only on some speeds or not at all.
issues.why: Toyota issued a heater performance bulletin for the 1996 Tercel. On older cars, a failed blower motor resistor or blower motor is also a common cause.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. If the fan has missing speeds, the blower resistor is a likely fix. For weak heat, ask a dealer about the heater bulletin.

issues.t: Musty smell from the A/C vents
issues.sym: A sour or mildew smell when you first turn on the A/C or fan.
issues.why: Moisture on the A/C evaporator lets mold and bacteria grow. Toyota issued a bulletin about evaporator odor for this model year.
issues.next: Replace the cabin air filter if fitted, and run the fan with the A/C off for a few minutes before parking. A shop can clean the evaporator if the smell stays.

issues.sym: The engine cranks longer than normal before it starts.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for hard starting on the 1996 Tercel. Fuel pressure, ignition parts and a weak battery are the usual things to check.
issues.next: Have a shop check fuel pressure, spark and battery voltage, and ask a Toyota dealer about the hard-start bulletin for this year.

issues.t: Check engine light at high altitude (P0130/P0133)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with oxygen sensor codes while driving in the mountains, even though the car runs normally.
issues.why: The engine computer's logic could set false oxygen sensor codes at high altitude. Toyota revised the logic to stop the unneeded warnings.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the sensor tests good and you drive at altitude, ask a Toyota dealer about the bulletin before buying a new sensor.

issues.t: Oil pressure light flickers at idle
issues.sym: The red oil light flickers or comes on when the car is stopped at idle, then goes out when you drive off.
issues.why: Low oil level, thin or old oil, a worn oil pump or bearings, or a failing oil pressure switch can all cause low readings at idle on a high-mileage engine.
issues.next: Check the oil level right away and top it up. If the light stays on while driving, stop the engine and have it towed. Ask a shop to measure oil pressure with a gauge before replacing parts.

issues.sym: The battery is dead after the car sits, even after replacing the battery or alternator.
issues.why: Something is drawing power with the car off, or the charging system is not recharging the battery. Owners report replacing parts without finding the cause.
issues.next: Ask a shop for a charging-system test and a parasitic draw test before buying more parts. A draw test finds the circuit that is draining the battery.
